Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd

   or ParentProcessName endswith "\onenote.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\mspub.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\visio.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium

DeviceFileEvents

Hugging Face warns an autonomous AI agent hacked its network

BleepingComputer
2026-07-20 7 use cases 3 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

The Hugging Face artificial intelligence repository disclosed that attackers gained access to internal datasets and credentials after breaching its production infrastructure using an autonomous AI agent system. [...]

ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002 T1555.003

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] HuggingFace datasets worker RCE: Python dataset loader spawns shell/network tool · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Dataset worker beaconing to public staging services (self-migrating C2) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Cloud/cluster credential harvesting on Hugging Face dataset-processing worker · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
HuggingFace datasets worker RCE: Python dataset loader spawns shell/network tool AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the code-execution step of the Hugging Face breach where a malicious dataset abused a dataset-config template injection and a remote-code dataset loader (trust_remote_code) to run code on a processing worker. Surfaces a Python process whose command line references the datasets loading path spawning a shell or network utility child — behaviour a clean feature-extraction worker never exhibits. Rationale: Anchors on the article's two named code-exec paths (dataset-config template injection + remote-code dataset loader / trust_remote_code) by requiring the parent Python command line to reference the Hugging Face datasets loading machinery, then requiring a shell/network child — a combination legitimate ML feature-extraction workers do not produce.
ATT&CKT1203 T1059.006 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate dataset preprocessing scripts that shell out to git/curl to fetch external corpora
  • ML engineers running load_dataset interactively in a notebook and then invoking bash for data wrangling
  • Dataset builder scripts that call chmod on downloaded extraction binaries
  • CI pipelines that pip-install and then run shell hooks under the same python parent
  • Custom datasets with legitimate remote code that spawns tar/curl to assemble shards
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("pip install","conda","/opt/conda/bin") and FileName in~ ("chmod","tar"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full parent Python command line and the child process/args; identify which dataset repo/config was being processed and whether trust_remote_code was set. 2) Contain: kill the worker, quarantine/evict the node, and block the dataset repo from further processing; snapshot the container for forensics before rebuild. 3) Hunt: on the same host look for subsequent reads of ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.kube/config and outbound connections to public paste/hosting services (see companion UCs); rotate any cloud/cluster credentials that were resident on the worker.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python3.10","python3.11")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("load_dataset","trust_remote_code","datasets","dataset_infos","datasets_modules")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","nc","ncat","chmod","base64","python","python3")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("python","python3")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("load_dataset","trust_remote_code","datasets","dataset_infos","datasets_modules")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","nc","ncat","chmod","base64")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cloud/cluster credential harvesting on Hugging Face dataset-processing worker AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the credential-theft stage of the breach: after code execution on a processing worker, the attacker read cloud and cluster credentials to move laterally across internal clusters. Surfaces processes touching AWS credential files, kubeconfig, git credentials, or Kubernetes service-account tokens on a dataset worker. Rationale: Directly targets the article's 'steal cloud and cluster credentials and move laterally across several internal clusters' step by keying on the exact on-disk credential artifacts (AWS creds, kubeconfig, k8s SA tokens, git creds) read by generic file-read/exfil tools on a worker that has no operational reason to touch them.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.005 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • kubectl / aws-cli legitimately reading ~/.kube/config or ~/.aws/credentials during operator maintenance
  • In-cluster pods with legitimate access to /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io service-account tokens
  • Backup or config-management jobs (Ansible) tar'ing home directories that include credential files
  • CI runners echoing masked credentials from ~/.git-credentials for git operations
  • Developer debugging cat'ing their own AWS config on a shared jump host
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kubectl","aws","helm","ansible-playbook") and ParentProcessName !in~ ("python","python3","sh","bash"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the process lineage — was the reader spawned by the datasets Python worker (link to the RCE UC)? Identify which credential files were touched and their scope. 2) Contain: immediately revoke and rotate the specific AWS keys, kube service-account tokens, and git credentials resident on that node; invalidate active sessions/roles they could assume. 3) Hunt: pivot into CloudTrail/AKS audit for use of those credentials from unexpected source IPs, and check other worker nodes for the same credential-read pattern indicating swarm-wide harvesting.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".aws/credentials",".aws/config",".kube/config","kubeconfig",".git-credentials","serviceaccount/token","/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io")
| where FileName in~ ("cat","cp","tar","curl","base64","grep","python","python3","sh","bash","dd","head")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (".aws/credentials",".aws/config",".kube/config","kubeconfig",".git-credentials","serviceaccount/token","/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("cat","cp","tar","curl","base64","grep","python","python3","sh","bash","dd","head")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Dataset worker beaconing to public staging services (self-migrating C2) AICommand & Control Low
Hunts the command-and-control stage described as 'self-migrating command-and-control staged on public services'. Surfaces a Python/dataset processing worker or its shell children reaching out to public paste/hosting/tunnel services that a feature-extraction worker should never contact. Rationale: Targets the article's explicit 'self-migrating command-and-control staged on public services' phrasing by watching for a Python/dataset worker (which should only reach HF-internal and dataset-source hosts) resolving/connecting to well-known public paste, tunnel and object-drop services abused for resilient C2.
ATT&CKT1102 T1071.001 T1568.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate dataset scripts pulling shards from raw.githubusercontent.com or a gist
  • Package tooling fetching wheels/config from Cloudflare Workers or Pages-hosted mirrors
  • Engineers using transfer.sh / 0x0.st to move a debug artifact off a worker
  • CI pipelines posting build status to a Discord webhook
  • Model cards or dataset READMEs referencing pastebin content fetched by a loader
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("pip install","huggingface_hub","git clone") and RemoteUrl has "raw.githubusercontent.com")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full URL/domain, the initiating process command line, and whether the same worker showed the RCE or credential-read patterns; extract bytes-out to gauge exfil vs beacon. 2) Contain: block the destination at proxy/egress, isolate the worker, and preserve the process and network capture before rebuild. 3) Hunt: look for the C2 'migration' — the same worker or sibling sandboxes rotating to a second public service after the first is blocked, and correlate resolved IPs across the short-lived sandbox fleet to map the swarm.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","curl","wget","sh","bash","nc","ncat")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("pastebin.com","raw.githubusercontent.com","gist.githubusercontent.com","workers.dev","pages.dev","trycloudflare.com","transfer.sh","0x0.st","termbin.com","ngrok","discord.com/api/webhooks")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DnsQuery has_any ("pastebin.com","raw.githubusercontent.com","gist.githubusercontent.com","workers.dev","pages.dev","trycloudflare.com","transfer.sh","0x0.st","termbin.com","ngrok")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: e9d4b217-3a86-4c05-8f1b-7c02a9e6d334
description: Detects a Python/shell process on a data-processing worker resolving public paste, tunnel or hosting services used to stage self-migrating C2.
references:

logsource:

detection:

| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app IN ("python","python3","curl","wget","sh","bash") AND (All_Traffic.dest_host="*pastebin.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*raw.githubusercontent.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*gist.githubusercontent.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*workers.dev" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*pages.dev" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*trycloudflare.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*transfer.sh" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*0x0.st" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*termbin.com") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.app IN ("python","python3","curl","wget","sh","bash") AND (All_Traffic.dest_host="*pastebin.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*raw.githubusercontent.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*gist.githubusercontent.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*workers.dev" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*pages.dev" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*trycloudflare.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*transfer.sh" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*0x0.st" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*termbin.com") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",

   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"

Critical

New 7-Zip Vulnerability Could Let Crafted XZ Archives Run Code During Extraction

The Hacker News
2026-07-20 14 use cases 7 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Opening a crafted XZ archive in 7-Zip could let an attacker run code on the machine. The flaw, CVE-2026-14266, is a heap-based buffer overflow in how the archiver processes XZ chunked data, and Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative (ZDI) detailed it on July 15. A fix shipped on June 25 in 7-Zip 26.02. The overflow lets an attacker "execute code in the context of the current process," per the

CVEsCVE-2026-14266 CVE-2026-48095
ATT&CKT1021.001 T1190 T1195.002 T1486 T1528 T1555.003 T1566

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Vulnerable 7-Zip (<26.02) exposed to CVE-2026-14266 / CVE-2026-48095 heap overflows
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Inbound XZ archive attachment delivered — CVE-2026-14266 delivery vector · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] 7-Zip process (7z/7zFM/7zG) spawning shell or LOLBin child — post-exploit of XZ/NTFS heap overflow · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
7-Zip process (7z/7zFM/7zG) spawning shell or LOLBin child — post-exploit of XZ/NTFS heap overflow AIExploitation Medium
Hunts successful exploitation of CVE-2026-14266 (XZ MixCoder_Code heap overflow) or CVE-2026-48095 (NTFS handler overflow), where code executes in the context of the 7-Zip process. A 7-Zip GUI/CLI binary spawning cmd/PowerShell/mshta/rundll32 etc. is anomalous — normal archive handling does not launch interpreters or LOLBins. Rationale: Anchored on the exact 7-Zip binary set (7z.exe/7zFM.exe/7zG.exe/7za.exe) that the advisory says the exploit executes within ("context of the current process"); a 7-Zip parent spawning an interpreter/LOLBin has near-zero legitimate baseline. Corroborated the code-in-process-context and vulnerable-version facts via Rescana and IT-Connect. Cross-checked against: • https://www.rescana.com/post/cve-2026-14266-critical-7-zip-xz-archive-decoder-vulnerability-enables-remote-code-execution-patch-in-26-02 • https://www.it-connect.tech/7-zip-vulnerability-why-you-should-install-version-26-02-now/ • https://socprime.com/blog/cve-2026-48095-7-zip-heap-overflow-flaw/
ATT&CKT1203 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User opens a 7-Zip SFX (self-extracting) archive that legitimately launches a setup command via cmd.exe
  • Analyst/sandbox detonating archives during malware triage
  • Developer double-clicking a .bat/.cmd inside an archive via 7-Zip 'Open inside' view
  • IT packaging scripts invoked through 7-Zip GUI RunAs context
  • Software installers bundling 7-Zip that shell out to a post-extract configure step
Suppression filter
| where not (FileName =~ "cmd.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("7zSfx","7zS.sfx","7zS2.sfx"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the child ProcessCommandLine and the archive path the 7-Zip parent had open; check whether the child is an interpreter with download/exec args or an unexpected LOLBin, and whether the source archive was a .xz/.7z from email or Downloads. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the child process tree, and quarantine the source archive; capture the 7z parent's open file handle/path for the malicious sample. 3) Hunt: sweep the same host and org for subsequent 7z*-parented network egress, new persistence (Run keys, scheduled tasks) written within minutes, and other recipients of the same archive hash/filename.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("7z.exe","7zFM.exe","7zG.exe","7za.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","cmstp.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildProcess = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("7z.exe","7zFM.exe","7zG.exe","7za.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\cmd.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\cmstp.exe","\\bitsadmin.exe","\\certutil.exe","\\curl.exe")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable 7-Zip (<26.02) exposed to CVE-2026-14266 / CVE-2026-48095 heap overflows AIWeaponization High
Surfaces every managed endpoint still running a 7-Zip build affected by the XZ decoder overflow (CVE-2026-14266) or the NTFS-handler overflow (CVE-2026-48095), both rolled up in 7-Zip 26.02. 7-Zip updates are manual installs from the official site, so set-and-forget machines will not self-patch — this is the primary article-driven exposure hunt. Rationale: Uses the two concrete CVE IDs named in the article (CVE-2026-14266, CVE-2026-48095) and the fixed build (26.02); cross-sourced the vulnerable range 21.07–26.01 and the 26.02 rollup from Rescana/IT-Connect and the CVE-2026-48095 GHSL-2026-140 advisory. If TVM has not yet mapped the fresh CVEs, pivot to software-inventory filtering SoftwareName has '7-zip' and SoftwareVersion below 26.02. Cross-checked against: • https://www.rescana.com/post/cve-2026-14266-critical-7-zip-xz-archive-decoder-vulnerability-enables-remote-code-execution-patch-in-26-02 • https://www.it-connect.tech/7-zip-vulnerability-why-you-should-install-version-26-02-now/ • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-48095
ATT&CKT1203
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Portable/standalone 7-Zip copies TVM already re-scanned as patched but cached at old version for <24h
  • Third-party product bundling its own vulnerable 7-Zip DLL reported under the vendor's software name, not '7-Zip'
  • p7zip/7-Zip forks (NanaZip, 7-Zip-zstd) that share the code but carry different version strings
  • Version string with 4-part build (e.g. 26.01.0.0) confusing naive semver comparison in the inventory fallback
  • Machines already patched to 26.02 but pending a reboot/rescan
Response runbook
1) Triage: rank hosts by exposure — internet-facing, high-privilege users, and machines that routinely open external archives first; confirm the installed SoftwareVersion is genuinely <26.02. 2) Contain: push 7-Zip 26.02 via your software-deployment tool (manual .exe from 7-zip.org — not auto-updating); where deployment lags, apply a temporary block/allow-list or file-association change for .xz/.7z opened from mail/Downloads. 3) Hunt: for any still-vulnerable host, correlate against UC 'XZ archive attachment' and '7-Zip spawning shell' hits to prioritise any host that both is vulnerable and recently opened an XZ archive.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-14266","CVE-2026-48095")
| where SoftwareName has "7-zip"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| sort by DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-14266","CVE-2026-48095")
| where SoftwareName has "7-zip"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| sort by DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Vulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities where (Vulnerabilities.cve IN ("CVE-2026-14266","CVE-2026-48095")) OR (Vulnerabilities.signature="*7-Zip*" AND Vulnerabilities.signature="*26.0*") by Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.signature Vulnerabilities.cve Vulnerabilities.severity | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)` | sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Vulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities where (Vulnerabilities.cve IN ("CVE-2026-14266","CVE-2026-48095")) OR (Vulnerabilities.signature="*7-Zip*" AND Vulnerabilities.signature="*26.0*") by Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.signature Vulnerabilities.cve Vulnerabilities.severity | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)` | sort - count
Inbound XZ archive attachment delivered — CVE-2026-14266 delivery vector AIDelivery Low
Flags delivered inbound email carrying an .xz / .txz / .tar.xz attachment, the specific archive type that triggers the CVE-2026-14266 XZ-decoder heap overflow when opened in a vulnerable 7-Zip. XZ archives are uncommon in routine business mail, so a delivered .xz to a non-developer recipient is a worthwhile lead — especially when correlated with the exposure and process-spawn UCs. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact exploitation prerequisite — a crafted XZ archive opened by the victim — matching .xz/.txz/.tar.xz attachment names on inbound-delivered mail. Sentinel left empty: the canonical Sentinel tables here (OfficeActivity) do not carry attachment filenames, so attachment-name detection is only expressible on Defender XDR's EmailAttachmentInfo. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/new-7-zip-vulnerability-could-let.html • https://www.rescana.com/post/cve-2026-14266-critical-7-zip-xz-archive-decoder-vulnerability-enables-remote-code-execution-patch-in-26-02
ATT&CKT1566.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer/DevOps teams receiving legitimate .tar.xz source tarballs from OSS vendors or CI systems
  • Linux/kernel or firmware distribution emails that routinely attach .xz payloads
  • Internal automation or build systems mailing compressed logs as .xz
  • Vendor patch/SDK deliveries packaged as .tar.xz
  • Security researchers sharing sample archives
Suppression filter
| where not (RecipientEmailAddress has_any ("dev@","devops@","build@","ci@","release@"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: check whether the recipient is a developer/role that normally receives .xz, inspect the sender domain reputation/SPF-DKIM, and detonate the attachment in a sandbox with a vulnerable 7-Zip build to confirm malicious XZ chunk framing. 2) Contain: if malicious, purge the message from all recipient mailboxes (soft/hard delete), block the sender/domain and attachment hash, and confirm target endpoints are on 7-Zip 26.02. 3) Hunt: pivot recipients into UC '7-Zip spawning shell/LOLBin' within minutes of delivery, and search for the same attachment SHA256 or filename across other inbound mail.
EmailAttachmentInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName endswith ".xz" or FileName endswith ".txz" or FileName endswith ".tar.xz"
| join kind=inner (
    EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where EmailDirection == "Inbound" and DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
    | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderMailFromDomain, DeliveryLocation
  ) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, SenderMailFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, FileName, FileType, DeliveryLocation
| order by Timestamp desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
EmailAttachmentInfo
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where FileName endswith ".xz" or FileName endswith ".txz" or FileName endswith ".tar.xz"
| join kind=inner (
    EmailEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where EmailDirection == "Inbound" and DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
    | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderMailFromDomain, DeliveryLocation
  ) on NetworkMessageId
| project TimeGenerated, SenderFromAddress, SenderMailFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, FileName, FileType, DeliveryLocation
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Email.All_Email where (All_Email.file_name="*.xz" OR All_Email.file_name="*.txz" OR All_Email.file_name="*.tar.xz") AND All_Email.direction="inbound" by All_Email.src_user All_Email.recipient All_Email.subject All_Email.file_name All_Email.message_id | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)` | sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Email.All_Email where (All_Email.file_name="*.xz" OR All_Email.file_name="*.txz" OR All_Email.file_name="*.tar.xz") AND All_Email.direction="inbound" by All_Email.src_user All_Email.recipient All_Email.subject All_Email.file_name All_Email.message_id | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)` | sort - count

| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",

SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Russian-Speaking Hacker Uses Google Gemini CLI to Control Botnet of Eight Dental Clinic PCs

The Hacker News
2026-07-20 16 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A solo Russian-speaking threat actor known as "bandcampro" outsourced a chunk of their operations to Google's open-source Gemini CLI artificial intelligence (AI) and commandeered a live botnet. The findings come from an analysis of 200 Gemini CLI session logs between March 19 and April 21, 2026, which found the threat actor using AI, among other things, to crack passwords, set up a residential

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] PowerShell one-liner pulling agent from Cloudflare tunnel (/api/v1) and IEX-executing · [LLM] PowerShell-created WMI permanent event subscription persistence (bandcampro agent) · [LLM] Scheduled task masquerading as OneDrive update running PowerShell (bandcampro agent) · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] PowerShell 5-second HTTPS beacon to Cloudflare tunnel C&C (bandcampro botnet) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
PowerShell 5-second HTTPS beacon to Cloudflare tunnel C&C (bandcampro botnet) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the bandcampro/Patriot-Bait botnet agent, a PowerShell script that checks in to a Cloudflare-tunnel-fronted C&C over HTTPS every 5 seconds to pull and run commands. Detection keys on powershell.exe/pwsh.exe as the originating process for repeated, high-cadence connections to *.trycloudflare.com / *.cfargotunnel.com, which no legitimate workstation script produces. Rationale: Anchors on the corroborated agent behaviour (5s HTTPS polling, Cloudflare-tunnel C&C) with the powershell.exe process pivot the article makes explicit; a scripting engine beaconing to trycloudflare.com dozens of times per 5-min window is not legitimate. Cross-checked Trend Micro, HelpNetSecurity and BleepingComputer for the interval and tunnel detail. Cross-checked against: • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/26/g/actor-behind-patriot-bait-used-ai-to-deploy-c2-botnet.html • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/07/16/jailbroken-google-gemini-cli-botnet/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/google-gemini-cli-abused-as-a-hacking-agent-malware-botnet-operator/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1572 T1102
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running `cloudflared tunnel` locally and testing an API via a PowerShell script against their own *.trycloudflare.com quick tunnel
  • CI/automation health-check scripts that poll a Cloudflare-tunnel-hosted internal service
  • Security team red-team or C2-emulation exercise using Cloudflare quick tunnels
  • A monitoring PowerShell task legitimately configured against a Cloudflare Zero Trust app on cfargotunnel.com
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("cloudflared.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the beaconing host, extract the full RemoteUrl/RequestURL set — confirm a fixed ~5s cadence and a /api/v1 path, and dump the powershell.exe command line + parent. 2) Contain: network-isolate the host, block the trycloudflare.com/cfargotunnel.com FQDN and resolved IPs at the proxy/firewall, kill the PowerShell agent process. 3) Hunt: sweep all endpoints (esp. the other 7 in the same subnet/clinic) for the same tunnel FQDN, then check for WMI event-subscription and OneDrive-named scheduled-task persistence and any OpenDental/DB access from the beaconing user.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(3d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has "trycloudflare.com" or RemoteUrl has "cfargotunnel.com"
| summarize Beacons = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Paths = make_set(RemoteUrl, 8), DstIPs = make_set(RemoteIP, 8)
    by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
| extend WindowSeconds = datetime_diff('second', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| where Beacons >= 20   // ~5s polling => ~60 conn / 5min; 20 is well above ad-hoc script noise
| order by Beacons desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(3d)
| where DestinationHostName has "trycloudflare.com" or RequestURL has "trycloudflare.com"
| summarize Beacons = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), URLs = make_set(RequestURL, 8)
    by SourceIP, DestinationHostName, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Beacons >= 20   // 5s HTTPS polling cadence; well above human browsing to one host
| order by Beacons desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe) @DestinationHostname:(*trycloudflare.com OR *cfargotunnel.com)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/trycloudflare\.com$/i ContextImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(as=Beacons))
| Beacons >= 10
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.app="powershell.exe" OR All_Traffic.process_name="powershell.exe" OR All_Traffic.process_name="pwsh.exe") AND (All_Traffic.dest_host="*.trycloudflare.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*.cfargotunnel.com" OR All_Traffic.url="*trycloudflare.com*") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.process_name span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where count>=20 | sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.app="powershell.exe" OR All_Traffic.process_name="powershell.exe" OR All_Traffic.process_name="pwsh.exe") AND (All_Traffic.dest_host="*.trycloudflare.com" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*.cfargotunnel.com" OR All_Traffic.url="*trycloudflare.com*") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest_host All_Traffic.process_name span=5m | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where count>=20 | sort - count
PowerShell one-liner pulling agent from Cloudflare tunnel (/api/v1) and IEX-executing AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the 'one-line PowerShell command to infect a machine' the actor generated: a powershell.exe invocation that downloads from a *.trycloudflare.com C&C (often a /api/v1 path chosen to blend with OpenAI-compatible traffic) and pipes the response to Invoke-Expression. Malware used no encoding/obfuscation, so the download+exec strings appear in cleartext on the command line. Rationale: Uses the article's explicit 'one-line PowerShell command to infect a machine' plus the corroborated cleartext (no obfuscation) download+run pattern and the /api/v1 OpenAI-mimicking C2 path from HelpNetSecurity; trycloudflare.com in a powershell command line is the high-fidelity anchor. Cross-checked against: • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/07/16/jailbroken-google-gemini-cli-botnet/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/google-gemini-cli-abused-as-a-hacking-agent-malware-botnet-operator/
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1105 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer testing an app hosted on their own Cloudflare quick tunnel via a one-off PowerShell fetch
  • Red-team/purple-team exercise staging tooling over trycloudflare.com
  • Internal automation that legitimately pulls a script from a Cloudflare-tunnel-hosted artifact endpoint
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("cloudflared.exe","code.exe","devenv.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full command line and the downloaded URL/path; note whether a /api/v1 endpoint on trycloudflare.com is referenced and grab the parent process. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block the FQDN + resolved IP, and preserve the on-disk agent script if written. 3) Hunt: pivot on the trycloudflare FQDN across all endpoints, then look for the follow-on 5s beacon (UC1) and WMI/scheduled-task persistence (UC3/UC4) on the same host.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "trycloudflare.com"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest","iwr ","Invoke-RestMethod","irm ","DownloadString","Net.WebClient","IEX","Invoke-Expression","/api/v1")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine has "trycloudflare.com"
| where CommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest","iwr ","Invoke-RestMethod","irm ","DownloadString","IEX","Invoke-Expression","/api/v1")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PowerShell Download-and-Execute From Cloudflare Tunnel C2
id: 8f2a1c7e-4d3b-4c9a-9e10-2b6f1a0d7c55
description: Detects powershell.exe downloading from a trycloudflare.com C2 and piping to Invoke-Expression, matching the bandcampro/Patriot-Bait botnet agent.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/russian-speaking-hacker-uses-google.html
    - https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/07/16/jailbroken-google-gemini-cli-botnet/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/21
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1105
    - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_img:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_c2:
        CommandLine|contains: 'trycloudflare.com'
    selection_exec:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX'
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
            - 'Invoke-RestMethod'
            - '/api/v1'
    condition: selection_img and selection_c2 and selection_exec
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe) @CommandLine:*trycloudflare.com* AND (@CommandLine:*IEX* OR @CommandLine:*Invoke-Expression* OR @CommandLine:*DownloadString* OR @CommandLine:*Invoke-WebRequest* OR @CommandLine:*Invoke-RestMethod* OR @CommandLine:*/api/v1*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| regex("trycloudflare\.com", field=CommandLine)
| CommandLine=/(iex|invoke-expression|downloadstring|invoke-webrequest|invoke-restmethod|iwr|irm|\/api\/v1)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, CommandLine], function=count())

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="powershell.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pwsh.exe") AND Processes.process="*trycloudflare.com*" AND (Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*" OR Processes.process="*IEX*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-WebRequest*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-RestMethod*" OR Processes.process="*/api/v1*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | sort - lastTime

PowerShell-created WMI permanent event subscription persistence (bandcampro agent) AIInstallation High
Hunts the admin-context persistence used by the bandcampro botnet: a WMI permanent event subscription (EventFilter + CommandLine/ActiveScript EventConsumer + FilterToConsumerBinding) created via PowerShell/WMIC to relaunch the C&C agent. The WMI event-consumer class names in a command line are rare and high-fidelity. Rationale: Directly targets the corroborated 'WMI event subscriptions' persistence (admin context) reported by HelpNetSecurity/BleepingComputer; the __EventFilter/EventConsumer/FilterToConsumerBinding class tokens are almost never seen in benign command lines, making this near-zero FP. Cross-checked against: • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/07/16/jailbroken-google-gemini-cli-botnet/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/google-gemini-cli-abused-as-a-hacking-agent-malware-botnet-operator/
ATT&CKT1546.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SCCM/MECM or monitoring agents (e.g. some SolarWinds/Nagios plugins) that register WMI event consumers for inventory
  • A sysadmin PowerShell script legitimately creating a WMI subscription for logon/event automation
  • EDR/DLP product installers that set up their own WMI event consumers
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ccmexec.exe","monitoringhost.exe","wmiprvse.exe") or ProcessCommandLine has "trycloudflare.com"
Response runbook
1) Triage: dump the full WMI subscription (Get-WmiObject -Namespace root\subscription -Class __FilterToConsumerBinding/EventFilter/EventConsumer) on the host and inspect the consumer's CommandLineTemplate/ScriptText for PowerShell/trycloudflare payloads. 2) Contain: delete the malicious EventFilter, EventConsumer and binding; isolate the host. 3) Hunt: check the same host and peers for the 5s Cloudflare beacon (UC1) and OneDrive-named scheduled task (UC4), and review who/what created the subscription (parent process, user).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wmic.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("__EventFilter","CommandLineEventConsumer","ActiveScriptEventConsumer","__FilterToConsumerBinding")
    or ProcessCommandLine has "Register-WmiEvent"
    or (ProcessCommandLine has "Set-WmiInstance" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("EventFilter","EventConsumer","FilterToConsumerBinding"))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has_any ("__EventFilter","CommandLineEventConsumer","ActiveScriptEventConsumer","__FilterToConsumerBinding","Register-WmiEvent")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Scheduled task masquerading as OneDrive update running PowerShell (bandcampro agent) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the non-admin persistence used by the bandcampro botnet: a scheduled task disguised as a 'OneDrive update' whose action launches PowerShell / an HTTP-fetching payload rather than the legitimate OneDrive updater. Keys on schtasks /create or Register-ScheduledTask referencing 'OneDrive' with a powershell/http/trycloudflare action, which the genuine OneDrive updater (OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe) never does. Rationale: Targets the corroborated non-admin persistence: a 'scheduled task disguised as a OneDrive update' (HelpNetSecurity). Requiring a powershell/http/trycloudflare action plus excluding the real OneDrive updater process separates it cleanly from the legitimate OneDriveStandaloneUpdater task. Cross-checked against: • https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/07/16/jailbroken-google-gemini-cli-botnet/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/google-gemini-cli-abused-as-a-hacking-agent-malware-botnet-operator/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1036.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legit 'OneDrive Standalone Update Task' — but its action is OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe, not powershell/http (filtered)
  • Admin packaging script that wraps OneDrive deployment in a PowerShell-invoked scheduled task
  • Endpoint management tooling creating an update task whose display name contains 'OneDrive'
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has "OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe" and InitiatingProcessFileName has "OneDrive")
Response runbook
1) Triage: export the task (schtasks /query /tn <name> /xml or Get-ScheduledTask) and inspect the Action — a powershell.exe/http/trycloudflare command confirms malice; note the creating user/process. 2) Contain: disable and delete the task, isolate the host, block any C2 FQDN it references. 3) Hunt: correlate to the 5s Cloudflare beacon (UC1) and WMI subscription (UC3) on the same host, and search all endpoints for scheduled tasks named 'OneDrive*' with non-OneDrive binary actions.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName =~ "schtasks.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/create")
    or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "Register-ScheduledTask")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "OneDrive"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("powershell","pwsh","trycloudflare.com","http")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("OneDriveSetup.exe","OneDrive.exe","OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName endswith "schtasks.exe" and CommandLine has "/create")
    or (NewProcessName has "powershell" and CommandLine has "Register-ScheduledTask")
| where CommandLine has "OneDrive"
| where CommandLine has_any ("powershell","pwsh","trycloudflare.com","http")
| where ParentProcessName !has "OneDrive"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Scheduled Task Masquerading as OneDrive Update Running PowerShell
id: b17e9f04-6c22-4a8d-9f31-5d7a0e2c8b41
description: Detects creation of a scheduled task named/disguised as a OneDrive update whose action launches PowerShell or an HTTP fetch, matching the bandcampro/Patriot-Bait botnet non-admin persistence.
references:

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
